title: Give the launch-template authority a typed context-insertion slot so rendered Foundation context reaches the provider
description:
FILED BY governor-f2db8452 ON EXPLICIT HUMAN INSTRUCTION, 2026-08-22. Governors do not plan and do not normally file; the human directed this row after the measurement below, and the branch it takes is the one task-933605a5 itself pre-authorizes.

WHY IT IS THIS ROW AND NOT A COMMENT (human filing bar, 2026-08-22): the gap is production-reachable, on committed bytes, and UNDEFENDED — no live arm, no owner row, and two independent lanes have already recorded it in committed prose without anyone owning the fix. task-933605a5's unblock text offers exactly two branches, "9a1eb61d's deliverable OR an explicitly filed recipe prerequisite". Branch one is spent: task-9a1eb61d is DONE and its producer shipped no slot. This row is branch two.

MEASURED AT COMMITTED HEAD 9c09252. Every command below is unpiped, so the exit codes are git's own and not a tail's:

1. THE AUTHORITY HAS NO CONTEXT CONCEPT AT ALL.
   git grep -n -i -E "insertion|contextSlot|contextManifest|renderContext|contextDigest" -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-authority.ts   -> exit 1, zero lines
   git grep -n -i "context" -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-authority.ts                                                              -> exit 1, zero lines
   The bare-word grep is the stronger one: the string "context" does not occur anywhere in the authority file. Same result on the producer half:
   git grep -n -i -E "insertion|contextSlot|contextManifest|renderContext|contextDigest" -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts  -> exit 1, zero lines
   This reproduces governor-7211ec87's 14:48Z measurement at 16c6230 and my own at d4e92c5, so the reading is stable across ten-plus commits. NOTE FOR THE PLANNER: the earlier measurements greped only launch-template-producer.ts; the authority was split out into launch-template-authority.ts and must be measured too. Both are clean.

2. THE INPUT IS A CLOSED, EXACT-KEYS CONTRACT — SO THIS IS A REFUSAL, NOT AN OMISSION.
   launch-template-producer.ts:74  export interface LaunchTemplateInput { capabilities; mission; runtimeObservation }
   launch-template-producer.ts:80  const INPUT_KEYS = Object.freeze(["capabilities", "mission", "runtimeObservation"])
   launch-template-producer.ts:83  const MISSION_KEYS = Object.freeze(["instructions", "test", "title", "workspace"])
   launch-template-producer.ts:114 if (!hasExactKeys(input, INPUT_KEYS)) { ...refuse... }
   launch-template-producer.ts:121 `producer input is exactly ${INPUT_KEYS.join(", ")}`
   Rendered context bytes cannot be smuggled through as an extra key: hasExactKeys REFUSES the call. There is no seam to widen incrementally and no positional back door — the argv is built positionally by design ("never built by iterating a record: key iteration order is a latent instability", producer comment above RESUME_FLAGS).

3. THE RENDERER EXISTS; NOTHING CALLS IT.
   packages/context/src/context-render.ts:57  export function digestContextManifest(...)
   packages/context/src/context-render.ts:64  export function renderContext(...)
   git grep -rn "renderContext" -- apps/daemon/src ':!*.test.ts' ':!*fixtures*'  -> exit 1, ZERO production consumers.
   So the daemon can render context and never does. That is the whole defect in one line.

4. THE DEPENDENCY EDGE IS ALREADY THERE — this row does NOT need a manifest edit.
   apps/daemon/package.json dependencies includes "@moe/context": "workspace:*".
   The edge still has to be PROVEN at plan time per the workspace-edge global rail (manifest + lock importer + self-deleting compiled bare-specifier probe); it just will not need creating.

5. CORROBORATION FROM THE OTHER END OF THE LANE, committed production prose, same HEAD:
   apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-handoff.ts:26  " `contextDigest` still has no producer. That remains a relay, disclosed."

WHAT THIS BLOCKS. Four CRITICAL rows are serial behind it: this row -> task-933605a5 (prelaunch composition; its condition 3 is exactly this slot) -> task-203a5ca7 (persist the exact attempt context manifest; where contextDigest gets a durable producer) -> task-a20e8ef6 (nine-key scheduler ReleaseHandoff builder) -> task-89838d72 (strand-free UNPROVEN release, parked to BACKLOG 2026-08-22). task-933605a5's blockedReason is STALE IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION — its clauses 1 and 2 (task-c320c34a, task-225d25f7) are now both DONE, so a reader who checks only those concludes the block is over. Clause 3 is this row. See comment-2ac14ada on task-933605a5.

DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-JUDGED HERE: the slot's exact name, its arity, whether it carries rendered bytes plus a digest or a reference to a committed manifest record, and whether the producer or a caller performs the render. The planner chooses on measured grounds and says why. What is NOT open: it must be a TYPED, NAMED slot. Positional argv guessing is forbidden, and reinterpreting mission.instructions to carry context is forbidden — task-933605a5's own rail and the 2026-08-22 15:03Z governor ruling both refuse it, and the launch-template authority is where that refusal has to hold.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK FIRST, at the delivered tree, before any other step. Re-run all four measurements UNPIPED and record command plus exit code in planningNotes.codebaseInsights: (a) `git grep -n -i "context" -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-authority.ts` and (b) the same over launch-template-producer.ts still return zero lines exit 1; (c) `git grep -rn "renderContext" -- apps/daemon/src ':!*.test.ts' ':!*fixtures*'` still returns zero production consumers; (d) INPUT_KEYS is still the frozen exact-keys triple behind `hasExactKeys` at producer:114. If ANY of these has landed since filing, REPORT THE COLLISION and block rather than reimplementing it — a silent duplicate in a shared worktree collides with its owner. Piped runs report the tail's exit code and are not admissible evidence here.

A TYPED, NAMED context-insertion slot exists on the launch-template input contract and is carried through to the produced launch fields. The slot is named in the frozen INPUT_KEYS (or in an explicitly-named nested exact-keys record), so the exact-keys discipline at producer:114 is PRESERVED, not relaxed: an unknown extra key must still refuse. Positional argv insertion is forbidden; reinterpreting or concatenating into `mission.instructions` to carry context is forbidden and must be shown to still refuse.

The bytes the slot carries are produced by the real `@moe/context` renderer through its owning production reader — `renderContext` / `digestContextManifest` at the package's public root — never re-implemented, re-derived, or hand-built inside the daemon or inside a test helper. A test that constructs the rendered value itself does not discharge this clause. If the render cannot be reached from the launch path without a prerequisite this row does not own, file that prerequisite symbol-by-symbol and block; do not stub it.

Every missing, malformed, oversized, foreign-attempt or unrenderable context input refuses CLOSED with a stable reason code and layer, and forwards any upstream sourceCode/sourceLayer UNRESTAMPED. Per epic rail 6 the tests assert the specific code AND which layer refused — not merely that the call failed. A refusal-only suite is not sufficient: at least one arm must prove a correct context value is ACCEPTED and reaches the produced fields, or the refusal arms are answerable by a guard that rejects everything.

The `@moe/daemon` -> `@moe/context` edge is PROVEN, not assumed, even though `apps/daemon/package.json` already declares `"@moe/context": "workspace:*"`: record (a) the manifest entry, (b) the pnpm-lock.yaml importer entry for the consumer, and (c) a compiled probe inside apps/daemon importing from the BARE specifier `@moe/context` that typechecks exit 0, with the probe deleted in the same command. A root-barrel grep does not satisfy this.

MUTATION DRILLS, each applied ALONE, each naming the test that must go RED, each restored byte-exact — `git diff -- <file>` empty for tracked paths, SHA-256 equality against an out-of-tree %TEMP% backup (suffixed by worker id, verified in a call SEPARATE from the restore) for any untracked path, with `git status --porcelain` on the exact mutated paths taken BEFORE drilling: (a) remove the slot from the frozen key list — the acceptance arm must red; (b) let an unknown extra key through `hasExactKeys` — the exact-keys refusal arm must red; (c) point the slot at a foreign attempt's rendered context — the identity-binding arm must red. ANY GREEN DRILL IS A VACUOUS ASSERTION: strengthen the arm, re-run, and say so in a row comment rather than recording a pass.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` is EXIT 0 on a fresh run with the `Test Files N passed` COUNT LINE quoted — an exit-0 leg with no count line ran nothing and is UNVERIFIED. Foreign uncommitted red at gate time is attributed by path with `git status --porcelain` plus an `it(` title diff of HEAD vs worktree and reported verbatim; never edit or revert another lane's bytes. Load-bearing evidence goes in a row comment via moe.add_comment, NEVER in the completion summary — that field is write-only and is persisted nowhere on the record.
taskRails: Scope is the context-insertion SEAM in the launch-template authority (apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts and launch-template-authority.ts) and the minimum wiring that carries rendered context into it. Do NOT persist a context manifest here — that is task-203a5ca7. Do NOT compose the prelaunch flow here — that is task-933605a5. Do NOT touch the release/handoff lane (a20e8ef6, 89838d72) at all.

The slot must be TYPED and NAMED. Positional argv guessing is forbidden. Reinterpreting, appending to, or overloading `mission.instructions` to smuggle context is forbidden — task-933605a5's rail and the 2026-08-22 15:03Z governor ruling both refuse it, and this authority is where that refusal must hold.

Preserve the exact-keys discipline. `hasExactKeys` refusing unknown keys is a load-bearing property of this producer, not an obstacle: widen the contract by naming the new key, never by loosening the check. A change that makes the producer tolerant of arbitrary keys is a rejection, even if every new arm passes.

Fail closed with stable reason codes; forward upstream sourceCode and sourceLayer UNRESTAMPED; missing or unverifiable context stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority. Never synthesize rendered context the renderer did not produce.

Use TDD. Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400 — this cap is PER FILE, never per task, and there is no net-LOC budget. Preserve foreign uncommitted WIP in the shared worktree; stage and commit only explicit owned paths; never git add -A, reset, or stash.

implementationPlan.description: DoD-0 VERIFY-OR-BLOCK, at YOUR delivered tree, before anything else. Run each command UNPIPED and record the command AND its exit code in the step note — a piped run reports the tail's status and is inadmissible here. (a) `git grep -n -i "context" -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-authority.ts` must return ZERO lines, EXIT 1. (b) the same over `apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts` must return ZERO lines, EXIT 1. (c) `git grep -rn "renderContext" -- apps/daemon/src ':!*.test.ts' ':!*fixtures*'` must return ZERO production consumers, EXIT 1. (d) `git grep -n "INPUT_KEYS\|hasExactKeys" -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts` must still show the frozen triple at :80 and the gate `hasExactKeys(input, INPUT_KEYS)` at :114. **If ANY has landed since filing, REPORT THE COLLISION and block — do not reimplement someone's landed work in a shared worktree.** Then confirm the two facts this plan rests on, which the filing did not measure: `packages/context/src/index.ts:2` is `export * from "./context-render.js"` (so `renderContext`/`digestContextManifest` are root-reachable — a NAME grep on index.ts returns nothing because of the star re-export; do not misread that as unpublished), and `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-context-selection.ts:125` still calls `selectContext` in production (so the renderer's input is reachable and DoD-2 needs no prerequisite). Record baselines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, counts read from the OUTPUT. Record the tree state and name any foreign dirty path.

TDD RED — write every arm first in apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.test.ts, extending the existing suite's shape. THE ACCEPTANCE ARM IS THE ONE DoD-3 REQUIRES AND IT MUST COME FIRST, because a refusal-only suite is answerable by a guard that rejects everything: (1) ACCEPTED — build a real `AdmittedContextSelection`, call the REAL `renderContext` from the bare specifier `@moe/context` to get `{bytes, manifest}`, pass it in the new slot, and assert the producer ACCEPTS and that the produced fields carry the rendered value through VERBATIM (deep-equal against the renderer's own output object, never against a literal). DoD-2 is explicit that a test constructing the rendered value itself does not discharge the clause — the value must come from `renderContext`. (2) EXACT-KEYS PRESERVED — an unknown extra key on the input still refuses `LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_INPUT_INEXACT` + layer (rail 2's load-bearing property). (3) SLOT MISSING — input without the slot refuses with the new code + layer. (4) MALFORMED SLOT — slot present but not the exact `{bytes, manifest}` record, and `manifest` not the exact `{version, binding, digest}` record: refuse + layer. (5) DIGEST MISMATCH — take a REAL rendered value and alter one field of `manifest.binding` while leaving `manifest.digest` untouched: refuse the digest code + layer. This is the anti-forgery arm. (6) BYTE SUBSTITUTION — swap `bytes` for different bytes while leaving `manifest` (including `binding.exactBytes`) intact: refuse. (7) UNSUPPORTED VERSION — `manifest.version` not `CONTEXT_MANIFEST_VERSION`: refuse + layer. (8) FORBIDDEN SMUGGLING PATH STILL REFUSES (rail 1, DoD-1) — a mission whose `instructions` carries rendered context text is NOT admitted as context: assert the produced fields carry no context from that route, and that `mission` still admits through `MISSION_KEYS` unchanged. Every refusal arm asserts the exact code AND which layer refused (epic rail 6). Run focused — RED, each red named with its reason.

GREEN 1 — THE ADMISSION HELPER, in apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-authority.ts beside `admitCapabilities` (:85), which is the established home for admission in this seam. Add to the CLOSED frozen roster `LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_PRODUCER_CODES` (:15-26) the new codes — suggested `LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_CONTEXT_INVALID` (slot absent, not an exact `{bytes, manifest}` record, manifest not an exact `{version, binding, digest}` record, or binding not the renderer's exact 7-key record) and `LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_CONTEXT_UNVERIFIED` (the digest recompute or the bytes/`exactBytes` comparison failed). Keep `PRODUCER_LAYER` MODULE-PRIVATE and published only as the closed TYPE — the file's own comment at :28-32 explains that an exported column-zero `*_LAYER` owes the security roster a hostile trio, and this row must not create that debt. Export `admitRenderedContext(value: unknown)` returning the admitted `RenderedContext` or a refusal: it exact-keys `{bytes, manifest}`, exact-keys the manifest, checks `manifest.version === CONTEXT_MANIFEST_VERSION`, **recomputes `digestContextManifest(manifest.binding)` using the PACKAGE's own function imported from the bare specifier `@moe/context` and refuses unless it equals `manifest.digest`**, and asserts `binding.exactBytes` equals `bytes` element-wise (both are `readonly number[]`, so compare length then values — `===` is reference equality and would pass a substituted copy). Document in one comment why the recompute is the mechanism: a rendered value the real renderer did not produce cannot carry a digest that recomputes, which is what makes DoD-2's "never hand-built" a property rather than a promise.

GREEN 2 — THE SLOT ON THE CONTRACT, in apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts. Add the NAMED key to the frozen `INPUT_KEYS` (:80) — suggested `renderedContext`, making it a four-key roster — and add the matching typed field to `LaunchTemplateInput` (:74) as `readonly renderedContext: unknown` (the exact-keys admission is what types it, consistent with the other three). **Do not touch `hasExactKeys` or the gate at :114**: the contract widens by naming the key, never by loosening the check (rail 2 — a producer made tolerant of arbitrary keys is a rejection even if every new arm passes). In `compose`, call `admitRenderedContext(input.renderedContext)` alongside the existing admissions, forwarding its refusal unchanged; if the admitted value carries an upstream code/layer, forward it UNRESTAMPED via the existing `LaunchTemplateUpstream` shape (:37) rather than minting a producer code over it (rail 3). Carry the admitted value onto the produced fields: add `readonly renderedContext: RenderedContext` to `LaunchTemplateFields` (:62) and include it in the frozen return at :160-162, verbatim — the producer is a carrier here, not a transformer. Make step 2's arms 1 and 3-7 green. Keep the file under the 250-line target (174 today).

GREEN 3 — PROVE THE EDGE, which DoD-4 requires as evidence and not as an assumption even though the manifest entry already exists. Record all three: (a) `apps/daemon/package.json` declares `"@moe/context": "workspace:*"`; (b) the `pnpm-lock.yaml` importer entry for `apps/daemon` carries `@moe/context`; (c) a COMPILED PROBE inside `apps/daemon` that imports `renderContext` and `digestContextManifest` from the BARE specifier `@moe/context` and typechecks EXIT 0, **with the probe deleted in the same command**. A root-barrel grep does not satisfy this clause and neither does the fact that the test file imports it. Note in the step why the probe matters here specifically: the symbols are published via `export *`, so a name grep on the package index proves nothing about what a bare import actually resolves.

MUTATION DRILLS (DoD-5) — each applied ALONE, each naming the test that must go RED, each restored byte-exact with `git diff -- <file>` EMPTY verified in a SEPARATE call, and `git status --porcelain` on the exact mutated paths captured BEFORE drilling. (a) REMOVE THE SLOT from the frozen `INPUT_KEYS` — the ACCEPTANCE arm must red. (b) LET UNKNOWN KEYS THROUGH — relax the `hasExactKeys(input, INPUT_KEYS)` gate at :114 — the exact-keys refusal arm must red (this is rail 2's property, drilled). (c) FOREIGN CONTEXT — point the slot at a rendered context built from a DIFFERENT selection while leaving the digest self-consistent — the arm that binds the carried value to what was supplied must red; if nothing reds, the acceptance arm is only checking shape and must be strengthened to compare against the renderer's own output object, and say so. (d) SKIP THE RECOMPUTE — delete the `digestContextManifest` comparison — the DIGEST MISMATCH arm must red. (e) TRUST `bytes` — delete the `binding.exactBytes` comparison — the BYTE SUBSTITUTION arm must red; **if it stays GREEN that arm was vacuous** (the two comparisons can mask each other) and must be strengthened before proceeding. (f) LOCAL DIGEST — replace the package's `digestContextManifest` with a local sha256 over the binding — an arm must red, proving the daemon is not re-deriving the renderer's authority. **ANY GREEN DRILL IS A FINDING, not a pass: strengthen the arm, re-run, and record it in a row comment rather than logging a pass.**

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW before the gate. Read the diff as an attacker. Can a caller reach the produced fields with context the renderer never made — via a proxy or a throwing getter (the producer's `try/catch` at :165 answers `LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_INPUT_HOSTILE`; confirm the new admission is inside that boundary)? Does an EMPTY `bytes` array with a matching digest admit, and should it — state the decision in the module rather than leaving it to the first caller who renders an empty selection. Are `bytes` and `binding.exactBytes` compared by VALUE and not by reference? Does any refusal path leak the caller's own text back out (the producer deliberately does not echo caught error messages — keep that)? CHECKLIST: no column-zero `*_LAYER` export added to the authority file; the new codes are on the closed frozen roster so `refuse()` type-checks them; `hasExactKeys` itself is unmodified; `grep -n "instructions" apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts` shows no new read of mission.instructions; both production files under the 250-line target; no new module and therefore no new `.js` bridge needed (both bridges already exist); no debug or scratch files.

GATE, COMMIT, RECORD. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` on a FRESH run, EXIT 0, with the `Test Files N passed` COUNT LINE quoted verbatim — an exit-0 leg with no count line ran nothing and is UNVERIFIED (DoD-6). Also run `pnpm test:security`: this row adds entries to an exported code roster, and that suite has its own tsconfig and vitest config and is reached by no other leg. Attribute foreign uncommitted red by path with `git status --porcelain` plus an `it(` title diff of HEAD vs worktree, report it verbatim, and never edit or revert another lane's bytes. COMMIT by explicit pathspec of exactly the three owned files. **PUT LOAD-BEARING EVIDENCE IN A ROW COMMENT via moe.add_comment, NEVER in the completion summary — DoD-6 says that field is write-only and persisted nowhere.** The comment must state: (1) the slot's final name, arity and shape, and WHY the renderer's own output type was chosen over a manifest reference (nothing persists a context manifest yet — that is task-203a5ca7, blocked behind this row); (2) that the digest recompute plus the `exactBytes` comparison are what make "never hand-built" mechanical, with the drill names that prove each; (3) per-drill RED test names; (4) the edge probe evidence and that it was deleted in the same command; (5) **THE CROSS-ROW HAZARD: `LaunchTemplateFields` now has a FIFTH field. `produceLaunchTemplateFields` has zero production consumers today so nothing reds, but task-fc9660b0 composes these fields into the 7-key attempt template and task-dbaec2b1's plan asserts set-equality over "the producer's four fields". Both planners must learn about the fifth field from this record rather than from a gate failure.** (6) task-933605a5 recorded as the consumer — its condition 3 is exactly this slot.

comments.content:
LOAD-BEARING EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW, in a comment because DoD-6 says the completion summary is write-only and persisted nowhere. Commit 2adc7dc, four files, no foreign bytes.

(1) THE SLOT: FINAL NAME, ARITY AND SHAPE, AND WHY THIS TYPE.
`renderedContext`, a fourth NAMED key on the producer's frozen `INPUT_KEYS` (`["capabilities","mission","renderedContext","runtimeObservation"]`), typed `readonly renderedContext: unknown` on `LaunchTemplateInput` and carried onto `LaunchTemplateFields` as `readonly renderedContext: RenderedContext`. Arity one; the value is the package's own `RenderedContext` = exactly `{bytes, manifest}`, manifest exactly `{binding, digest, version}`, binding exactly the renderer's seven bound fields.

WHY THE RENDERER'S OUTPUT TYPE AND NOT A REFERENCE TO A COMMITTED MANIFEST: nothing persists a context manifest yet. That is task-203a5ca7, which is blocked BEHIND this row, so a reference slot would point at a record that cannot exist and this row would have to invent a store to satisfy its own contract. Carrying the renderer's own value is the only shape that is checkable today. When 203a5ca7 lands, the slot can gain a durable reference alongside the bytes without changing the key.

WHY THE EXACT-KEYS DISCIPLINE IS PRESERVED RATHER THAN RELAXED: the contract widened by NAMING the key. `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts | grep -E "^[-+].*hasExactKeys"` returns NOTHING - not one line of the gate changed. That grep is the falsifiable form of rail 2 and is cheaper than reading the diff.

(2) WHAT MAKES "NEVER HAND-BUILT" MECHANICAL RATHER THAN A PROMISE.
Two independent checks, and they catch disjoint attacks:
- `digestContextManifest(binding) === manifest.digest`, recomputed with the PACKAGE's own function imported from the bare `@moe/context`. Nothing in the daemon re-derives a sha256 or the canonical encoding.
- `sameBytes(bytes, binding.exactBytes)` element-wise. `===` would have been vacuous: `renderContext` assigns the SAME array to both (context-render.ts:75, :82), so a reference check passes on every honest value AND on every substituted copy.
Drill (d) proves the first, drill (e) the second, drill (f) proves the recompute is the package's and not a local one.

A version check sits BEFORE the digest and is separate from it, because `digestContextManifest` seals the CONSTANT version, not the manifest's own field - a tampered `manifest.version` still recomputes to the stored digest, so the recompute can never answer for it. The test arm asserts that digest equality explicitly before asserting the refusal.

LIMIT, stated in the module and repeated here: the recompute proves the value passed through the package's sealer, NOT that the SELECTION behind it was this attempt's. A caller holding `@moe/context` can render an invented selection and seal it honestly. This is a FORGERY check, not a PROVENANCE one. Provenance needs the persisted manifest from task-203a5ca7.

(3) PER-DRILL RED TEST NAMES. Six planned drills plus one from adversarial review. Each applied ALONE; restore proven by SHA-256 against `%TEMP%\moe-drill-worker-934d8b66\` in a call SEPARATE from the restore (`git diff` was NOT usable - all four files were uncommitted at drill time, so an empty diff would have meant my work was gone).
(a) remove the slot from INPUT_KEYS -> 65 red. "ACCEPTS a context the real renderer produced and carries it through verbatim". COARSE by construction: dropping a key from an exact-keys roster reds every caller in the file, so it shows the key is load-bearing but discriminates weakly.
(b) relax the exact-keys gate to presence-only -> 4 red, incl. "still refuses an unknown extra key rather than widening to tolerate it". This is the falsifier for the ONE arm that was green at RED; without it that arm would have been an unfalsifiable regression guard.
(c) admission returns a value that is not the one supplied -> 4 red, incl. "carries the renderer's exact bytes, not a re-encoding" and "admits a foreign attempt's context as ITS OWN value". Proves the acceptance arm is not merely shape-checking.
(d) delete the digest recompute -> 1 red, exactly "refuses a binding edited under a digest that was not recomputed". The narrowest mutant the arm title claims.
(e) delete the `exactBytes` comparison -> 2 red, incl. the named "refuses bytes swapped under an untouched manifest". Second red is explicable: `sameBytes` is the only thing that READS `bytes`, so deleting it also stops the throwing-getter arm from reaching the hostile boundary.
(f) local sha256 instead of the package digest -> 37 red incl. the acceptance arm. Coarse for the right reason: swap the derivation and nothing admits.
(g) revert the prototype hardening -> 2 red, exactly the two new prototype arms. See (7).
NO GREEN DRILL. Nothing needed strengthening after the fact.

(4) EDGE PROBE. `apps/daemon/package.json:20` declares `"@moe/context": "workspace:*"`; `pnpm-lock.yaml:112` is the `apps/daemon:` importer and `:114` carries `'@moe/context'` with `version: link:../../packages/context` (nearest importer header computed, not eyeballed). A compiled probe inside `apps/daemon` importing `renderContext` and `digestContextManifest` from the BARE specifier typechecked EXIT 0 and was DELETED IN THE SAME COMMAND (`test -e` absent, and porcelain grep for `edge-probe` returns 0).

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL CAUGHT A FALSE PASS. My first probe was named `src/.edge-probe-*.ts` and a DELIBERATELY BROKEN version of it still exited 0 with the file unnamed in tsc output - TypeScript's `src/**/*.ts` glob does not match dot-prefixed files, so the probe was never compiled. Renamed without the dot, the broken probe correctly failed with
  `error TS2322: Type '(selection: AdmittedContextSelection) => RenderedContext' is not assignable to type 'number'`
which is also the strongest edge evidence here: an unresolved specifier gives TS2307, not a correct structural type. Had I run only the positive probe I would have recorded "typecheck EXIT 0" for a file tsc never opened.

(5) CROSS-ROW HAZARD - `LaunchTemplateFields` NOW HAS A FIFTH FIELD.
`{argv, environment, launchSelection, limits, ok, renderedContext}`. Two planners must learn this from here rather than from a gate failure:
- task-fc9660b0 composes these fields into the seven-key attempt template.
- task-dbaec2b1's plan asserts set-equality over "the producer's four fields".

WHAT THIS ROW PROVES:
- The launch-template seam ACCEPTS a rendered context only if it passed through `@moe/context`'s own sealer: `digestContextManifest(binding)` recomputes to `manifest.digest`, and `bytes` equals `binding.exactBytes` element-wise. That is an ANTI-FORGERY and internal-consistency property. A record this daemon hand-built, edited, or re-derived cannot satisfy it, and my drills confirm both halves bite independently.
- The suite reaches that seam with a value the PRODUCTION renderer minted (production `selectContext` then production `renderContext`), so DoD 3's "never re-implemented, never hand-built, not constructed by a test helper" is discharged for the value under test.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, and must not be cited as:
- **Provenance.** It does not prove the production launch path obtained its bytes from THIS attempt's real selection. Anyone holding `@moe/context` can render a selection it invented and seal that honestly; the seal is truthful about the renderer, not about whose selection it was. `LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_CONTEXT_UNVERIFIED` names exactly that boundary, and `launch-template-authority.ts` states it in its own header comment ("this admission is a forgery check, not a provenance one") — I am recording it here so the boundary lives on the row too, not only in the source.
- **Composition.** Nothing here shows a production caller assembling the slot on the real prelaunch path. `produceLaunchTemplateFields` still has zero production consumers at the delivered tree; this row is the SEAM, and the composition is `task-933605a5`'s.
- **Durable selection identity.** Binding a launch to a selection the store actually recorded needs a persisted context manifest, which is `task-203a5ca7`'s deliverable and does not exist yet.

FOR DOWNSTREAM PLANNERS (`933605a5`, `203a5ca7`, `fc9660b0`, `dbaec2b1`): treat `ee5a385b` as the typed slot plus a forgery check, never as origin proof. A plan that cites this row as evidence that launched context came from the attempt's own selection is citing it for something QA did not verify and the code does not claim.
